title: Setting Up a New Printer
cardText: Set up a new printer on a Windows computer using USB, Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
Configure wireless printing from the printer control panel, a mobile app or the manufacturer's PC installer.
Install suitable printer drivers and confirm the printer works with a test page.
text: This guide helps you connect and install a new printer on a Windows computer.
It covers USB and network printers, including several ways to configure Wi-Fi.
The exact setup procedure varies by printer manufacturer and model.
Before starting, unpack the printer, remove shipping materials, install the ink or toner, load paper and turn it on.
Follow the connection method you intend to use.

chooseConnection.title: Are you connecting the printer directly by USB?
body: Decide whether the printer will connect directly to your computer using a USB cable or through your network.
For Wi-Fi or Ethernet printing, choose No.
For a permanent USB connection, choose Yes.

connectUsb.title: Connect the printer using USB
body: Check that the printer supports a USB connection and that you have the correct cable.
Connect the USB cable between the printer and computer.
Turn on the printer and allow Windows to detect it.
Some manufacturers recommend connecting the USB cable only when their installer prompts you. Follow those instructions if applicable.
connectUsb.alt: Diagram showing a USB cable connecting a printer to a computer
connectUsb.caption: Example USB printer connection. The connector type varies by printer model.

checkUsbConnection.title: Check the USB connection
body: Confirm the printer is turned on and has no error messages.
Check that the USB cable is firmly connected at both ends.
Try another USB port and, if available, another compatible cable.
Avoid USB hubs and docking stations while diagnosing connection problems.
Check whether Windows detects the printer after reconnecting it.

checkNetworkConnection.title: Is the printer already connected to your network?
body: Check the printer screen, network status page or network configuration report.
For Wi-Fi, confirm the printer is connected to your normal wireless network.
For Ethernet, confirm the network cable is connected to the router or switch.
If the printer already has a working network connection, proceed to installing it on Windows.

checkControlPanel.title: Can you configure Wi-Fi from the printer control panel?
body: Check whether the printer has a screen or buttons for Wi-Fi or network settings.
Look for Wireless Setup, Wi-Fi Setup Wizard, WLAN or Network Settings.
If the printer supports wireless setup from its control panel, use that method first.
If it does not, check whether a manufacturer's mobile app can configure it.

setupWifiControlPanel.title: Connect the printer to Wi-Fi using its control panel
body: Open the printer's Wi-Fi or Network Settings menu.
Select Wireless Setup Wizard or the equivalent option.
Select your wireless network name (SSID).
Enter the Wi-Fi password carefully, checking uppercase and lowercase characters.
Wait for the printer to confirm the connection.
Some printers support only particular Wi-Fi bands or security modes, so check the model's network requirements if your network is not listed.

link.name: Brother wireless setup instructions
link.description: Official example of configuring Wi-Fi directly from a printer's control panel.

setupWifiControlPanel.alt: Brother printer screen showing the wireless network Setup Wizard
setupWifiControlPanel.caption: Example Wi-Fi Setup Wizard on a Brother printer. Menu names vary between manufacturers.

checkMobileApp.title: Does the manufacturer offer a mobile setup app?
body: Check whether the printer manufacturer provides a compatible mobile application for initial setup.
Examples include the HP app, Brother Mobile Connect and Epson Smart Panel.
Confirm that the application supports your exact printer model.
If a suitable app is available, use it to configure the printer.
Otherwise, try the manufacturer's PC installer.

setupMobileApp.title: Configure the printer using a mobile app
body: Install the manufacturer's official printer setup app on your phone or tablet.
Connect the phone to the wireless network you want the printer to use.
Turn on Bluetooth and allow the app's requested local network or location permissions when required for device discovery.
Put the printer into Wi-Fi setup mode if instructed.
Open the app, choose to add or set up a new printer and follow the instructions.
Wait for confirmation that the printer has joined your network.

link.name: HP printer setup using the HP app
link.description: Official HP instructions demonstrating mobile printer setup. Other manufacturers use different apps.

setupMobileApp.alt: HP mobile printer setup application showing the Add Printer options
setupMobileApp.caption: Example mobile printer setup interface. Use the application recommended for your printer model.

setupPcInstaller.title: Try the manufacturer's PC installation software
body: Find the printer model on the manufacturer's official support website.
Download the recommended Windows driver and installation software.
Run the installer and select the wireless or network installation option where available.
Follow the instructions for discovering or connecting the printer to Wi-Fi.
If the installer completes network setup successfully, continue to Windows printer installation.

link.name: Brother software and driver downloads
link.description: Find the correct software for a Brother printer. For other brands, use the manufacturer's official support website.

setupPcInstaller.alt: Brother support website showing the full driver and software package
setupPcInstaller.caption: Example full driver and software package. Download software for the exact printer model.

temporaryUsbSetup.title: Try temporary USB-assisted wireless setup
body: Some printers can use a temporary USB connection to configure their wireless network settings.
Check whether the manufacturer's installer supports this method for your printer model.
If supported, connect the printer to the computer with a USB cable when prompted.
Use the installer to select your Wi-Fi network and enter its password.
Wait for the installer to confirm the wireless connection.
Disconnect the USB cable only when the installer instructs you to do so.
temporaryUsbSetup.alt: USB cable connecting a printer to a computer during installation
temporaryUsbSetup.caption: A USB cable may be used temporarily to configure Wi-Fi on supported printers.

addPrinterWindows.title: Add the printer in Windows
body: Ensure the printer is switched on and connected to the same network as the computer, or connected by USB.
Open Windows Settings, then Bluetooth & devices, then Printers & scanners.
Select Add device and wait while Windows searches for available printers.
Select the correct printer and complete the installation.
If Windows cannot find the printer, try the manual printer installation option or install the manufacturer's driver.

link.name: Microsoft: Add or install a printer in Windows
link.description: Official Windows instructions for adding USB and network printers, including manual installation.

addPrinterWindows.alt: Windows 11 Printers and scanners settings showing the Add device button
addPrinterWindows.caption: Windows 11 printer settings. The appearance may vary with Windows updates.

installPrinterSoftware.title: Install or update the printer driver
body: Check whether Windows has already installed a suitable printer driver.
If a driver is missing or the printer is not working correctly, download the recommended driver from the manufacturer's website.
Install the correct model-specific driver and follow the setup instructions.
If the exact driver is unavailable, check whether the manufacturer offers a compatible universal printer driver.
A universal driver may provide only basic printing features and might not support scanning or other functions.
After installation, try printing a test page.

link.name: Microsoft printer installation instructions
link.description: Instructions for adding printers and obtaining suitable printer drivers through Windows.

testPrinter.title: Print a test page
body: Open Windows Settings and select Bluetooth & devices, then Printers & scanners.
Select the new printer.
Open Printer properties and choose Print Test Page.
Check that the printer produces the page correctly.
If it is a multifunction printer, also test scanning separately after the printer setup is complete.

printerSetupComplete.title: Printer setup complete
body: The printer has been installed and successfully prints from Windows.
If you use this printer regularly, consider setting it as your default printer.
For network printing, keep the printer connected to the correct network.
If the printer supports scanning, test that function separately.

setupUnable.title: Further printer setup troubleshooting required
body: The printer could not be installed or the connection could not be completed.
Confirm the exact printer model and whether it supports USB, Ethernet, Wi-Fi or Wi-Fi Direct.
Record any error messages from the printer, Windows or the manufacturer's installer.
Check the manufacturer's support documentation for model-specific setup requirements.
If the printer is installed but will not print, use the Cannot Print troubleshooting guide.
If the manufacturer's driver is unavailable, investigate supported universal drivers or Windows built-in drivers before replacing the printer.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix printer connection and printing problems
link.description: Troubleshooting steps for printers that Windows cannot connect to or print from.
